description: CROI-REPORTED: F_access x t_crit distribution-free bound as a RANGE at canonical W=34.5h
source_locator: envelope_bound_range(t_crit_h=34.5, eps_max_at_zero=0.95, F_median_h=96.0, GSD=2.0, eta=0.05) -> (F_access=0.0699132, lower=0.0664175, upper=0.1129219)
verification_method: run v3_revision/r3_pk_pd/test_envelope_bound_range.py; sections 2-4 must PASS (section 3 asserts upper end is bit-identical to envelope_bound())
notes: FIGURE REPORTED IN THE CROI 2027 ABSTRACT (Finite_Window_CROI.docx, Results). LOWER BOUND CONVENTION: assumes ZERO residual post-window protection (v4 gating rule - no drug acquired before t_crit implies E_PEP = 0). UPPER BOUND CONVENTION: preserves the prior eta=0.05 residual-efficacy convention, crediting eta to the (1-F_access) fraction that misses the window. The true bound lies between the two ends: someone initiating just past t_crit receives some efficacy, below eta by construction but above zero. Upper end is bit-identical to bound_envelope_par (0.11292185121039905). Added additively 2026-09-28; no existing computation, t_crit, or Monte Carlo output was altered.

notes: Single graphic submitted with the CROI 2027 abstract, in place of the three-panel S1 (CROI accepts multi-panel figures only where panels show the same analysis). Each row: F_access(W) from a log-normal access delay (median 96h, GSD 2.0); LOWER BOUND CONVENTION: assumes ZERO residual post-window protection (v4 gating rule - no drug acquired before t_crit implies E_PEP = 0). UPPER BOUND CONVENTION: preserves the prior eta=0.05 residual-efficacy convention, crediting eta to the (1-F_access) fraction that misses the window. The W=34.5h row is the canonical operating point and equals bound_envelope_par_range. NOTE the 60h lower bound is 23.6%, not 23.7%: recomputing from the DISPLAYED rounded F_access (0.249) gives 23.7%, but F_access(60) = 0.2488631 gives 23.6%. The artifact carries full precision. This is a sensitivity band, not a measured PWID exposure-to-initiation distribution.
